doc.title: Phoebe Jacobs and Jackie Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: The All-Stars' life on the road
summary: Jacobs says road life of 336 days a year was a passion, like Ellington's band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did his musicians in the All-Stars, were they able to keep up with the pace? I mean I know they had to but, how did they feel about that?

In those days it was no pace, it was a way of life. I mean if a musician was usually married, had some kids and if he was — the guys that Louis worked with cared about their music as much as he did. So living on the road and being out 336 days a year was nothing to them. Look at Duke, he did the same thing with his band. I mean that was the lifestyle then. If the musician was passionate and wanted it, that was his life, that’s what he did and he never thought about it any more than a doctor would think he’s overworking because he is taking care of sick people. If you’re passionate about what you’re going to do, that’s it.
